name: Dindigul Biryani
subtitle: small-grain rice, curd and a heavy hand with pepper, the biryani that tastes sour

ingredients.note: seeraga samba is traditional; the small grain is what holds the sourness
sourness is the signature here, so let the curd stand out
Dindigul leans on pepper where other biryanis use chilli

prepNotes: Three things separate Dindigul from its neighbours: sour curd, crushed pepper and the small seeraga samba grain.
Marinate in the refrigerator, not on the counter. An hour is plenty.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, ginger, garlic, pepper and salt for 1 hour in the refrigerator.
Fry the cinnamon and cloves in the oil, add the onion and fry until golden.
Add the green chillies, tomato and the marinated chicken. Cook until the oil separates, 12 minutes.
Add the water and mint, bring to a boil and check the seasoning. It should taste slightly over-salted.
steps.tip: The rice will absorb it. Season the liquid, not the finished dish.

steps.text: Stir in the washed rice, cover tightly and cook 15 minutes on the lowest heat.
Rest 10 minutes before opening and forking through.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Cool quickly and refrigerate within two hours. Reheat under a lid with a sprinkle of water.
